spec.title: PROP-074 — User project and per-project overrides: user-scoped packages, late boot lanes and user memory
spec.p: Framework record, owner request 2026-11-08. Status `spec/plan`: the shape below is decided, the details are settled during implementation, which follows the cache-stable SYSTEM prefix work (campaign node `USER-PROJECT`, after `SYS-PROMPT`). Nothing here is implemented yet.

p.USER-PROJECT-PURPOSE: A user installs specification packages (flows, skills, stacks and the like) for themselves, not for one repository, with `vibe install -g`. Those packages form a separate tree in a per-user project. Every agent session in any vibevm project also loads that tree last, so it works as an advanced, structured, versioned `MEMORY.md` that follows the user across projects and machines.

p.USER-PROJECT-ROOT: One per-user project under the vibe settings root, a full ordinary vibevm project: its own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibevm/vibedeps/`, and an authored `vibevm/vibespecs/` tree (PROP/FEAT documents, boot sources, a user boot snippet). It is compiled, checked and updated by the same machinery as any project; no second compiler or loader exists.

p.USER-PROJECT-REUSE: The existing service user project that `vibe install -g mcp:…` materialises (PROP-027 REG-USER-PROJECT-MATERIALISATION) is the precedent. Whether the two become one project or stay separate roots sharing one owner is decided at implementation time; either way a service scope is carried explicitly by the CLI, never inferred from a path.

p.USER-PROJECT-INSTALL: `vibe install -g` of a specification package targets the user project; application and MCP packages keep their current `-g` meaning. `vibe update -g`, `vibe uninstall -g`, `vibe list -g` and `vibe check -g` operate on it with the ordinary project laws (locked sources, rollback, cooperative stop).

p.USER-LANE-SEPARATE: The user project produces its own boot lane from its own compilation. A repository's boot lane never embeds or copies it, so a teammate who clones the repository gets the identical project boot and no trace of another person's user lane.

p.USER-LANE-LAST: The user lane is always loaded dynamically, after the static lane, after every entry of the project's boot index and after any live continuation the SYSTEM work defines; only the project override lane (§5), when present, loads after it. A project may not reorder either earlier.

p.USER-LANE-OUTSIDE-PREFIX: The user lane never participates in the project's cache-stable SYSTEM prefix (`SYSTEM-PROMPT-SPEC`): changing or installing a user package never changes the project prefix bytes or invalidates its cache. It may enter only the separate, git-ignored composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX.

p.USER-LANE-ABSENT-OK: A missing, empty or broken user project never blocks a project session: the session boots as without it and diagnostics say what was skipped and why.

p.USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE: Loaded last does not mean ranked highest. Project rules (commit discipline, safety, attribution) bind whatever the user lane says; a user-lane statement that contradicts a project rule is reported, not obeyed. The exact precedence wording is part of the implementation.

memory.title: 4. User memory goes into the user project

p.USER-MEMORY-DEFAULT: By default, the facts an agent would otherwise write into a harness memory file (a local `MEMORY.md`, an auto-memory directory or similar) are written into the user project's `vibevm/vibespecs/` instead, as ordinary authored records that the user lane then loads.

p.USER-MEMORY-OPT-OUT: The default applies unless the user has explicitly decided otherwise and said so in a durable place (for example a setting in the user project or a statement in its user snippet). When opted out, agents use whatever memory mechanism the user chose and this law does not apply.

p.USER-MEMORY-CLASSIFICATION: The project-memory discipline still holds: a fact another contributor needs to build, review or understand a project belongs in that project's repository, never in the user project. Only facts about the user — preferences, working style, machine facts, cross-project conventions — go to the user project.

p.OVERRIDE-PURPOSE: Owner extension 2026-11-08. Everyone works with a project the same way, as recorded in git; a user who wants to work differently in that project keeps their own way in a per-user, per-project override project instead of committing it to the shared repository. The global user project is the outermost override for every project. The model is three layers: project ← project override ← global user project, the same ladder `.vibe/registry.local.toml` → `vibe.toml` → `~/.vibe/registry.toml` already uses for registries, generalised to the whole project.

p.OVERRIDE-SHAPE: An override project is an ordinary vibevm project like the user project (§2): own `vibe.toml`, lock, `vibedeps` and authored `vibevm/vibespecs`, its own compilation and its own boot lane. It never writes the project's tracked files or its lock, and a teammate's clone is unaffected by it.

p.OVERRIDE-LOCATION: Owner decision 2026-11-08: stored under the user's home, keyed by a project binding (repository identity plus checkout, the same binding the user-local steward contexts use), so it survives a re-clone and is shared by worktrees of one project. It is never stored inside the checkout. How a user enables, creates and selects an override is configurable; those mechanics and the exact binding key are settled at implementation.

p.OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE: Owner decision 2026-11-08: on conflict the more specific layer wins — project < global user project < project override. A per-project choice beats the user's general preference, as git's local beats global. Lanes load in the same order, project first, then the global user lane, then the project override lane, so the most specific text comes last. Non-overridable project rules still bind every layer (OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE).

p.OVERRIDE-ADDITIVE: Overrides add freely: extra packages, flows, skills, preferences. Taking away or replacing project rules is allowed only for what the project marks as overridable; commit discipline, attribution, safety and anything unmarked can only be supplemented. A layer statement contradicting a non-overridable project rule is reported, never obeyed (extends USER-LANE-PRECEDENCE).

p.OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION: Each layer has its own lock and is resolved and compiled separately in this task; a package an override needs at a version different from the project's lives in the override's own tree. The override lane loads dynamically, like the user lane (USER-LANE-LAST), and never enters the project's own cache-stable prefix; the composed prefix of LAYERED-PREFIX is the one place where the layers join.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX: In scope of this task (owner decision 2026-11-08): one cache-stable boot prefix composed from project + global user project + project override, in the precedence order of OVERRIDE-PRECEDENCE, with resolution across the layers. The project layer, as the most shared and most stable bytes, comes first, so the project's own prefix stays a byte-identical leading part of the composed one. Without a user project or override the composed prefix equals the project prefix. Until a user composes layers, the separately loaded lanes of §3 and OVERRIDE-SEPARATE-RESOLUTION remain the behaviour.

p.LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION: The composed prefix is personal and must never be committed. It is written inside the project's own `vibevm/` tree, next to the project's boot files, so an agent that looks around the file it was given finds the neighbouring files of the actual project and not of some other directory. The directory is ignored by a `.gitignore` that vibe writes into that directory itself (ignoring everything in it, including itself), never by editing the repository's root `.gitignore`. `vibe check` reports the composed prefix or its directory as an error when git tracks it. The exact path is settled at implementation (a sibling of `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/`, for example `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/local/`).

p.OVERRIDE-NO-AI-NATIVE-ANCHORS: Owner decision 2026-11-08: shared project code never anchors to a local layer. Checks written in the AI-native languages (`spec://` references, `specmark` scopes and `#[spec]`-style annotations, coverage and status checks) may target only the project's own specifications and its declared dependencies — never the global user project or a project override. Otherwise code committed for everyone would cite specifications that a teammate's checkout does not have. The AI-native checkers refuse such a reference with a message naming the reference, the local layer it points into and the fix; a layer's own specifications are never counted toward the project's coverage or status. This needs an update of the AI-native packages (`org.vibevm.ai-native.core-ai-native`, the Rust and TypeScript language packages and their MCP servers) as part of this task.

p.LAYERS-IN-TREE: Owner request 2026-11-08: `vibe tree` (plain, console TUI and vibeterm views, PROP-036) shows all three layers correctly — which layer each package, document and boot lane comes from, the effective result after precedence, and what a more specific layer supplements or replaces — and lets the user switch override layers on and off: hiding a layer in the view, and enabling or disabling a layer for the project itself (which then drops out of loading and of the composed prefix). The plain and JSON forms carry the same layer attribution.

p.USER-PROJECT-OPEN: Open: the exact root path and its relation to the MCP service project; how an override is enabled, created and selected, and the exact project-binding key (§5); the composed-prefix path and how harnesses are pointed at it (LAYERED-PREFIX-LOCATION); how `-g` tells a specification package from an application package when a package is both; the exact hook by which a project boot index names the user lane (a generated dynamic entry with a `when` condition is the expected shape); how harnesses that read only one instructions file reach the user lane; the record layout and naming for agent-written memory facts; the opt-out setting; migration of an existing `MEMORY.md`; multi-machine sync (the user project is a git repository the user may push anywhere).
